evidence: A silicon atomic layer was grown on a carbon-terminated c(2 x 2) sample surface at 1050°C by Si,H, exposure whose partial pressure was 1 x 10^-6 Torr. After every 20 s Si,H, exposure, the gas supply was stopped, and the sample was cooled down to room temperature to observe surface reconstruction with LEED and surface composition with AES, and subsequently it was again raised up to 1050°C, followed by the gas supply.
